label: sprites/fw_spit.spr: a sludge spit that splashes, animated

againstClass.words: starts too bright: an attack in its envelope
does not end dark: a decay in its envelope

R1.reason: The frame is one flat light-grey disc on a dark ground. There is no splash: no spread, droplets, crown or drip. Nothing reads as a sludge spit that splashes, so the effect the brief names is not there.

R2.reason: The frame is 32 x 32, a size the measures confirm, and the disc fills it evenly. The brief gives no frame size, and a splash would have a lobed or spreading silhouette, not a round fill, so the shape is clearly off.

R3.reason: The colour is a neutral near-white grey. The brief asks for green-grey sludge, consistent with the water and the crawler, and nothing in the frame has that tint. It is clearly off but not a wholly wrong family, so 1 rather than 0.

R4.reason: The brief asks for an animated splash, but there is one frame, so the motion is absent. The measures fail the envelope for the explosion class: it starts bright (first 1, class range 0 to 0.22), peaks at frame 0 (class range 0.22 to 0.71), and does not end dark (last 1, class range 0 to 0.03). A measured must-have fails, so this cannot score 2.

R5.reason: The type (parallel) and format (additive) are plausible for a glow-like effect and no measure flags them. Whether the name and read-back match SPRITE_CLASSES cannot be confirmed from the picture, and the sprite fails R1 to R4, so this scores 1 rather than 2. Note that the picture's folder is named decoy, and the image matches the decoy's description: one disc per sprite. That is a reason to fail it, not to score it higher.
